title: A prime power passes through a factor the prime does not divide
statement: For a prime p, a natural b that p does not divide, an exponent c and any natural a: if p to the c divides a times b, then p to the c divides a.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.prime_pow_dvd_of_dvd_mul_of_not_dvd : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> ((x3 : And (AxNat.le (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0) (((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat.dvd x3 x0) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat x3 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (Eq.{1} AxNat x3 x0))))) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat.dvd x0 x1) -> False)) -> ((x5 : AxNat) -> ((x6 : AxNat.dvd (AxNat.pow x0 x2) (AxNat.mul x5 x1)) -> AxNat.dvd (AxNat.pow x0 x2) x5)))))))

notes: Induction on the EXPONENT, with `a` quantified inside the motive because the step replaces `a` by `a / p`. Euclid's lemma peels one `p` off `a` -- never off `b`, which the second hypothesis forbids -- and left-cancellation removes it from both sides. It deliberately does NOT route through `Nat.Coprime`: this prelude has `prime_coprime_pow_of_not_dvd` (a prime coprime to a POWER) and nothing giving coprimality of a prime POWER with anything, which is what `coprime_dvd_mul_right` would need. Primality is spelled inline (`2 <= p /\ forall d, d | p -> d = 1 \/ d = p`), matching `euclid_lemma`'s own convention; this prelude has no `Prime` predicate.
